physics_goals.value: Precisely quantify quark-gluon plasma properties via jet, heavy-flavor and quarkonium measurements in heavy-ion collisions

summary.plain: sPHENIX is a new, house-sized detector at Brookhaven's RHIC collider, built where PHENIX used to be, using a recycled magnet from the BaBar experiment to study the hot soup of quarks and gluons made in nuclear collisions.
summary.technical: sPHENIX: a 1,000 t hermetic heavy-ion collider detector at RHIC IP8, built as a successor to PHENIX around a reused 20-ton BaBar solenoid; received DOE CD-0 mission-need approval 2017-01-13, completed construction April 2023, commissioned with first Au+Au data in the 2023 RHIC run, released its first physics results 2025-07-18, and operated through RHIC's 25th and final run, which concluded 2026-02-06.

unique_capabilities.value: Reuses the 20-ton superconducting solenoid magnet originally built for the BaBar experiment at SLAC
